# CREATE PROCEDURE's IN arguments and variable scope:
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language.md
# strict_mode=FALSE checks syntax only; IN arguments are local variables.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_in(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET x = x + 1; SELECT x; END;
CALL scalars.proc_in(41)
=> "42"

DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 7;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_local(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET x = 99; END;
CALL scalars.proc_local(x);
SELECT x
=> "7"

# A typed NULL stays NULL on entry.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_null(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT x IS NULL; END;
CALL scalars.proc_null(NULL)
=> "true"

# Temporary tables created by a procedure live for the script, including its caller.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_temp(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN CREATE TEMP TABLE proc_rows AS SELECT x AS n; END;
CALL scalars.proc_temp(8);
SELECT n FROM proc_rows
=> "8"

# RETURN exits only the procedure. IN arguments accept expressions.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_return(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN RETURN; SELECT x; END;
CALL scalars.proc_return(1 + 2);
SELECT 5
=> "5"

# Syntax-only validation permits references resolved when the procedure is called.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_late() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT n FROM _SESSION.proc_late_rows; END;
CREATE TEMP TABLE proc_late_rows AS SELECT 9 AS n;
CALL scalars.proc_late()
=> "9"

# Procedure variables cannot read the caller's variables.
DECLARE caller_only INT64 DEFAULT 3;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_no_capture() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT caller_only; END;
CALL scalars.proc_no_capture()
=> error:

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_bad_arity(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT x; END;
CALL scalars.proc_bad_arity()
=> error:

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_bad_type(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT x; END;
CALL scalars.proc_bad_type(STRUCT(1 AS a))
=> error:

# GoogleSQL's procedure parser checks declarations even with strict mode disabled.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_bad_syntax() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT 1; DECLARE x INT64; END;
SELECT 1
=> error:

# The default project inside a procedure is its owner's project, including domain-scoped IDs.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS `example.com:proj`.proc_owner;
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `example.com:proj`.proc_owner.t AS SELECT 11 AS n;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE `example.com:proj`.proc_owner.read_table() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN CREATE TEMP TABLE proc_owner_rows AS SELECT n FROM proc_owner.t; END;
CALL `example.com:proj`.proc_owner.read_table();
DROP SCHEMA `example.com:proj`.proc_owner CASCADE;
SELECT n FROM _SESSION.proc_owner_rows
=> "11"

# CALL can nest, with each frame keeping its own arguments.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_inner(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT x + 1; END;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_outer(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN CALL scalars.proc_inner(x + 1); END;
CALL scalars.proc_outer(40)
=> "42"

# A procedure sees a caller-created temporary table, and its writes stay in the same script.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_write(x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN INSERT _SESSION.proc_write_rows VALUES (x); END;
CREATE TEMP TABLE proc_write_rows (n INT64);
CALL scalars.proc_write(4);
SELECT SUM(n) FROM proc_write_rows
=> "4"

# IN arguments support the documented ARRAY and STRUCT types, including NULL elements.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_struct(x STRUCT<values ARRAY<INT64>>)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SELECT x.values[OFFSET(1)] IS NULL; END;
CALL scalars.proc_struct(STRUCT([1, NULL] AS values))
=> "true"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_empty_array(x ARRAY<INT64>)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(x); END;
CALL scalars.proc_empty_array([])
=> "0"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_null_array(x ARRAY<INT64>)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SELECT x IS NULL; END;
CALL scalars.proc_null_array(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INT64>))
=> "true"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: a procedure does not inherit the default
# dataset for table resolution, even though it can read the caller's @@dataset_id value.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_default_dataset() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT MAX(a) FROM t; END;
SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
CALL scalars.proc_default_dataset()
=> error contains: Table "t" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table).

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_system_dataset() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT @@dataset_id; END;
SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
CALL scalars.proc_system_dataset()
=> "scalars"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: caller temporary SQL UDFs are visible.
CREATE TEMP FUNCTION caller_function(x INT64) AS (x + 1);
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_caller_function() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT caller_function(1); END;
CALL scalars.proc_caller_function()
=> "2"

# OUT and INOUT arguments, from CREATE PROCEDURE's documentation:
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language.md
DECLARE accumulator INT64 DEFAULT 0;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_add_delta(INOUT x INT64, delta INT64)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SET x = x + delta; END;
CALL scalars.proc_add_delta(accumulator, 5);
CALL scalars.proc_add_delta(accumulator, 3);
SELECT accumulator
=> "8"

# An OUT argument starts as NULL, and the caller's variable takes the last value assigned to it.
DECLARE v INT64 DEFAULT 5;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_out_null(OUT x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT x IS NULL; END;
CALL scalars.proc_out_null(v)
=> "true"

DECLARE v INT64 DEFAULT 5;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_out_last(OUT x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET x = 3; SET x = 4; END;
CALL scalars.proc_out_last(v);
SELECT v
=> "4"

# OUT and INOUT arguments take variables, each passed once.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_out_value(OUT x INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET x = 1; END;
CALL scalars.proc_out_value(1)
=> error:

DECLARE v INT64;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_out_twice(OUT x INT64, INOUT y INT64)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SET x = 1; END;
CALL scalars.proc_out_twice(v, v)
=> error:

# Procedures run dynamic SQL, with the parameters of its USING clause, resolving names against
# the procedure's project.
DECLARE v INT64;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_dynamic_into(OUT y INT64) OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT ? + 1' INTO y USING 1; END;
CALL scalars.proc_dynamic_into(v);
SELECT v
=> "2"

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS `example.com:proj`.proc_owner_dynamic;
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `example.com:proj`.proc_owner_dynamic.t AS SELECT 12 AS n;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE `example.com:proj`.proc_owner_dynamic.read_table()
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE TEMP TABLE proc_owner_dynamic_rows AS SELECT n FROM proc_owner_dynamic.t'; END;
CALL `example.com:proj`.proc_owner_dynamic.read_table();
DROP SCHEMA `example.com:proj`.proc_owner_dynamic CASCADE;
SELECT n FROM _SESSION.proc_owner_dynamic_rows
=> "12"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: a temporary function that a procedure declares
# belongs to the script, and so does the @@dataset_id that a procedure sets.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_call_function() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN CREATE TEMP FUNCTION declared_in_procedure() AS (1); SELECT declared_in_procedure(); END;
CALL scalars.proc_call_function()
=> "1"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_declare_function() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN CREATE TEMP FUNCTION declared_in_procedure() AS (1); END;
CALL scalars.proc_declare_function();
SELECT declared_in_procedure()
=> "1"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_read_set_dataset() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars'; SELECT @@dataset_id; END;
CALL scalars.proc_read_set_dataset()
=> "scalars"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_set_dataset() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars'; END;
CALL scalars.proc_set_dataset();
SELECT @@dataset_id
=> "scalars"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_set_dataset_tables() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars'; END;
CALL scalars.proc_set_dataset_tables();
SELECT MAX(a) FROM t
=> "3"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: the procedure itself does not resolve table names
# against the @@dataset_id it sets.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_set_dataset_own_tables() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars'; SELECT MAX(a) FROM t; END;
CALL scalars.proc_set_dataset_own_tables()
=> error contains: Table "t" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table).

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: an OUT argument that the procedure never assigns
# leaves the caller's variable NULL, and a procedure that fails leaves it unchanged.
DECLARE v INT64 DEFAULT 5;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_out_unassigned(OUT x INT64)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SELECT 1; END;
CALL scalars.proc_out_unassigned(v);
SELECT v
=> null

DECLARE v INT64 DEFAULT 5;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_out_failed(OUT x INT64)
OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE) BEGIN SET x = 1; SELECT ERROR('fail'); END;
BEGIN CALL scalars.proc_out_failed(v); EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN SELECT 0; END;
SELECT v
=> "5"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: so does the @@dataset_project_id that a
# procedure sets.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_set_dataset_project() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SET @@dataset_project_id = @@project_id; END;
CALL scalars.proc_set_dataset_project();
SELECT @@dataset_project_id = @@project_id
=> "true"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: a procedure reads the caller's
# @@dataset_project_id, the script's @@time_zone, and the @@error of its own handlers, and its
# dynamic SQL does not resolve table names against the caller's @@dataset_id.
SET @@dataset_project_id = @@project_id;
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_read_dataset_project() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT @@dataset_project_id = @@project_id; END;
CALL scalars.proc_read_dataset_project()
=> "true"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_read_time_zone() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT @@time_zone; END;
CALL scalars.proc_read_time_zone()
=> "UTC"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_read_error() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN BEGIN SELECT ERROR('fail'); EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT REGEXP_CONTAINS(@@error.message, r'^(Query error: )?fail( at \[.+\])?$');
END; END;
CALL scalars.proc_read_error()
=> "true"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_dynamic_tables() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT MAX(a) FROM t'; END;
SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
CALL scalars.proc_dynamic_tables()
=> error contains: Table "t" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table).

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: CREATE PROCEDURE rejects query parameters in the
# body, even without strict mode.
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_parameter() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT @p; END
=> error contains: Query parameter is not allowed in the body of procedure 'scalars.proc_parameter': @p
